players.note: Nakobe Dean showed up in Week 10, racking up five solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. The LB3 in fppg, Dean is locked in as a top-five option due to his sky-high upside and incredible consistency. Fire up the Raiders linebacker with confidence for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos.

Arvell Reese has been sensational and continues to chug along as an elite IDP weapon. The LB2 in fppg, Reese recorded four solos and nine assists in Week 10. He is locked in as a top-three option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Jordyn Brooks was back at it in Week 10, notching six solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Brooks has caught fire for fantasy managers, recording four straight spike weeks, putting him firmly back in the top-12 conversation. Tap Brooks as a strong LB1 play for what should be a busy afternoon against the Buffalo Bills in Week 11.

Nick Bolton was at it again in Week 10, tallying five solos, four assists, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Bolton has started to heat up for fantasy managers and is once again locked in as a top-12 option. Count him as one for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Sonny Styles stepped up in Week 10, tallying five solos, eight assists, and one tackle for loss. It was the sixth spike week for Styles in nine games played, putting him at LB16 in fppg. Continue to treat the rookie linebacker as a top-20 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football.

Roquan Smith was excellent in Week 10, tallying six solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Roquan has just three spike weeks on the season, but does have a few near misses. With that said, the Ravens linebacker can no longer be trusted as a locked-in top-five option and is now better viewed as a top-15 type who is part of the weekly LB1 conversation. Tap Roquan as a top-12 option for Week 11, thanks to a plus matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Devin Lloyd was excellent in Week 10, tallying five solos, four assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Outside of a couple of duds, Lloyd has been a locked-in top-five producer; the duds, however, dropped him to LB7 in fppg through 10 weeks of action. Fire Lloyd up as a top-10 option for a tasty Week 11 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Kaden Elliss went off in Week 10, racking up six solos, nine assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. The LB8 in fppg, thanks to multiple splash weeks, Elliss has missed time but has been an elite option when he has been healthy. Tap Elliss as a top-15 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Micah McFadden impressed in Week 10, tallying five solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. McFadden has been on fire since stepping in as the starter in place of the injured Tremaine Edmunds and deserves to be counted as a top-25 option for as long as he stays sizzling. Fire him up as an upside LB2 for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Cashman is locked in as a top-three option if he gets cleared in time for Sunday Night Football. The LB1 in fppg, Cashman is a must-start regardless of opponent.

Payton Wilson was back at it in Week 10, piling up nine solos and 10 assists for his third splash week of the season. Wilson is the LB10 in fppg and remains locked in as a top-15 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Start him everywhere.

CJ Allen stayed hot in Week 10, racking up three solos, six assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Allen has produced at a LB1 level since becoming a starter and should be counted as a top-15 option for as long as he is cooking. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Houston Texans.

Quay Walker stepped up in Week 10, generating four solos, four assists, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. It was the fifth spike week of the season for Quay, who has settled in as a top-25 option during the byes. Treat Walker as just that for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Dre Greenlaw was excellent in Week 10, tallying four solos, four assists, and 0.5 sacks. Dre has been a top-25 play when he has been healthy and on the field and should be treated as such for what is suddenly an exciting edition of Sunday Night Football between Greenlaw's San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings. Start Dre as a LB2 play.

Cedric Gray got his first start of the season in Week 10, responding with eight solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Gray started the season injured and lost his role to Cody Barton in the process but may have just wrestled it back with his standout performance against Jacksonville. Tap Gray is an LB1 option if he gets another start.

Eric Wilson stepped up in Week 10, tallying six solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Wilson matched his season high in solos with Blake Cashman sidelined and reminded fantasy managers why we stick with him through the peaks and valleys. Treat Wilson as an LB3 with LB2 upside for what should be a busy night against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday Night Football.

Drue Tranquill was back at it in Week 10, racking up six solos and three assists. Drue has five spike weeks on the season as a whole, but three of them have come in his last four games, putting Tranquill firmly in the top-25 mix, with or without the byes. Start Drue with confidence as an upside LB2 play for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Patrick Queen was at it again in Week 10, going off with five solos, nine assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Queen is on absolute fire for IDP managers, riding three straight splash weeks to LB20 in fppg through 10 weeks of action. Count the Steelers linebacker as a top-25 option for a tasty Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Demetrius Knight stepped up in Week 10, notching six solos, two assists, and one pass defended. Knight has been one of the better LB2 options and checks into Week 11 as the LB27 in fppg. Treat the Bengals linebacker as a top-20 option for Week 11, thanks to the heavy bye and a plus matchup against Washington on Monday Night Football.

Mack Wilson was at it again in Week 10, notching six solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Wilson has started to heat up for IDP managers with two spike weeks in his last three games, making him much more attractive as an LB3 option. The LB2 upside is real, but we will need to see a little more before he enters that conversation outside of a six team bye. With that said, count Wilson as a top-25 option for Week 11, thanks both to the heavy bye and the plus matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Devin Bush stepped up in Week 9, reeling off three solos, six assists, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Bush has just three spike weeks on the season, but has recorded one in back-to-back games, making him a potential top-25 option for the heavy bye. Treat him as such for a plus Week 11 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

Jake Hansen was excellent in Week 10, recording four solos and eight assists. Jake Hansen is set to step back into the starting lineup for the Houston Texans due to Azeez Al-Shaair being placed on IR. Hansen got a handful of starts earlier this season and established himself as a solid LB3 option when he is getting the requisite snaps. Fire him up as a top-236 option where needed for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night Football.

Andrew Van Ginkel showed up in Week 10, tallying three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Now second in the league with 8.5 sacks, AVG continues to prove his elite fit in Brian Flores' scheme. Van Ginkel has been hot, with 4.5 of his 8.5 sacks coming in his last three games. Fire AVG up as a top-15 option for a neutral Week 11 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Bryce Boettcher got another start in Week 10, but managed just one solo and six assists. Boettcher is a desperation LB4 play at best and probably should not be sniffing Week 11 lineups in 12 team leagues unless you play in an unusually deep league where you grabbed Bryce specifically as Akeem Davis-Gaither cover. ADG was placed on IR prior to Week 10, so Boettcher should be rostered, but you do not want to lay him until he shows some consistent LB3-level production.

Del'Shawn Phillips showed up in Week 10, racking up four solos, five assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Phillips had his best fantasy game of the season on a season-low in snaps and is expected to continue to see his role shrink in favor of Denzel Perryman, who was just activated off IR ahead of Week 10, but played just 13 percent of the snaps. Phillips is worth holding onto in 20+ team leagues, but should be left on benches for Week 11 wherever possible.

Mike Green was excellent in Week 10, reeling off four solos, two assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Green is suddenly up to 5.5 sacks on the season, with 3.5 of them coming in three of his last four games. The Ravens edge rusher deserves to be part of the top-25 conversation for Week 11. Count him as just that for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Cody Simon stepped up in Week 10, tallying four solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Simon played 53 percent of the snaps compared to 47 percent for Jack Gibbens, so we may be seeing a changing of the guard here. His expanded Week 10 role was performance based not injury based, so there is a chance Simon sees north of 60 percent in Week 11 as the new starter beside Mack Wilson. Simon is a LB3 option if he gets the start as expected.

Danny Stutsman showed up in Week 10, notching six solos and three assists on 61 percent of the snaps. Stutsman saw an expanded role after Pete Werner left the game with a hamstring injury and could be in line for Week 11 start if Werner cant receover in time. Stutsman is more LB4 than LB3, even with Werner out, but with six teams on bye, he still makes for a solid option. Start him where needed if Werner is ruled out for Week 11, as expected.

Jadeveon Clowney is set to get another start for the Texans due to Danielle Hunter being ruled out on the short week. Jadeveon was solid in his first start of the season, recording one solo, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended on 76 percent of the snaps. Tap Clowney as a DL3 option where needed.

Chop Robinson was excellent in Week 10, reeling off three solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Chop has just five sacks on the season but is heating up with at least one sack in three of his last four games. Tap Robinson as a DL3 with DL2 upside as long as he is cooking. Start him everywhere for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Nik Bonitto was excellent in Week 9, tallying two solos, one sack, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Bonitto is up to 4.5 sacks and should be counted as a top-15 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Jaelan Phillips stepped up in Week 10, racking up four solos, one assist, one sack, three tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery. Phillips is up to 3.5 sacks, with at least a half sack in four of his five games played. Jaelan is a DL2 option when he is actually on the field, but staying healthy continues to be an issue for the talented edge rusher. Tap Phillips as a top-25 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

DJ Wonnum stepped up in Week 10, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Wonnum is healthy and no longer has to deal with the threat of ceding snaps to Derrick Moore due to Aidan Hutchinson being lost for the year. Wonnum has a healthy five sacks on the season, but this is his first since back in Week 5. Tap Wonnum as a DL3 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.  Add the Lions edge rusher where needed.

Odafe Oweh was excellent in Week 10, tallying three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The rotational edge rusher is up to five sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of his last four games played. Oweh played 74 percent of the snaps in Week 10, his highest ttal since back in Week 1, but should go back down or the 65 percent range in Week 11. Count Odafe as a top-30 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Cincinatti Bengals.

Jonathan Greenard showed up in Week 9, posting one solo, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Greenard, who finally has a sack under his belt and has a favorable schedule down the stretch with Pittsburgh, Arizona, Indianapolis, Seattle, and Houston among others. Count him as a DL3 with DL1 upside for Week 11 and beyond. The Eagles are on bye, so he should be flying far enough under the radar that you can add him for a pittance, especially when we consider his proven DL1 talent and upside on a line that is still dangerous sans Jordan Davis.

T.J. Parker went off in Week 10, exploding for three solos, two assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Parker has started to heat up for the Bills, recording at least one sack in two of his last three games. The rookie edge rusher is up to 3.5 sacks and seems to be finding his footing at the right time for Bills fans and fantasy managers alike. Parker has worked his way into a more even rotation with Bradley Chubb and Greg Rousseau and is now firmly on the DL4 radar. Tap Parker as a DL3/4 option for a tasty Week 11 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

L.J. Collier stepped up in Week 10, tallying three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the second of the season for Collier, who is starting to heat up with a sack in two of his last three games. Tap Collier as a DL4/5 option due to both the heavy bye and the plus Week 11 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.
